title: Reading files from your phone — the one statement that confused, said plainly

steps.path: Phone → tap a file → the preview
steps.headline: Should a file preview on the phone open in a sealed box that cannot touch the rest of the app?
steps.today: On the desktop, a preview is drawn inside the app itself. A web page the assistant wrote, for example, runs right there in the app's own window.
steps.problem: On a phone browser, anything drawn inside the app can see what the app sees, including that you are signed in. A file made by a bad skill, or a web page the assistant saved from the internet, could then act as you: read conversations, send messages, download other files.
steps.proposal: Previews open through a second door on the same computer, sealed off from the app, the way a phone opens an email attachment in a separate viewer that cannot read your mail. Yes builds it sealed; you would notice only that the first preview takes a moment longer. No draws previews inside the app like the desktop does; I would push back, because the milestone brief you approved asked for the sealed version. Don't know: I build it sealed.
